style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The first psalm in the Psalter with a superscription, and the first tied to a specific crisis: David fleeing Jerusalem barefoot across the Kidron with his son Absalom's coup behind him and the whole country choosing sides (2 Samuel 15-17). The enemies are many -- the word repeats three times -- and their theology is the real attack: 'there is no salvation for him in God.' David's reply is not an argument but a description: You, O LORD, are a shield around me, my glory, the One who lifts my head. Then the psalm's most famous claim, made by a man with an army hunting him: I lay down and slept, I woke again, because the LORD held me up. That sleep is the whole doctrine of providence in one night. The prayer that follows is fierce -- rise, LORD; You have struck my enemies on the jaw and shattered the teeth of the wicked. Then the last line hands the private rescue back to everyone: salvation belongs to the LORD; Your blessing be on Your people. Three Selahs pace it like a man catching his breath.

1.text: A psalm of David, when he fled from his son Absalom. O LORD, how many are my adversaries! Many are those rising up against me.
1.amp: A Psalm [mizmor] of David, when he fled [barach] from [panim] Absalom [Abshalom] his son [ben]. LORD [YHWH], how are they increased [rabab] that trouble [tsar -- adversary, one who hems in] me! many [rav] are they that rise up [qum] against me.
1.notes: The Psalter's first superscription pins the psalm to 2 Samuel 15: be-vorcho (barach, H1272) mi-pne Abshalom beno (H6440, H53, H1121) -- in his fleeing from the face of his own son. mah-rabbu tsarai (H7231, H6862): the adversaries have MULTIPLIED, and rabbim qamim alai (H7227, H6965), many rising against me -- 'many' will sound three times in two verses.

2.text: Many keep saying about my soul, 'There is no salvation for him in God.' Selah.
2.amp: Many [rav] there be which say [amar] of my soul [nephesh], There is no help [yeshuah -- salvation] for him in God [Elohim]. Selah [selah].
2.notes: The attack that matters: en yeshuatah lo b-Elohim (H3444, H430) -- not 'he will lose' but 'God is finished with him'. Shimei's curse in prose form (cf. 2 Samuel 16:7-8). The first Selah (H5542) lets the accusation hang before the answer.

3.text: But You, O LORD, are a shield all around me -- my glory, and the One who lifts my head high.
3.amp: But You, O LORD [YHWH], are a shield [magen] for ['about', the KJV margin] me; my glory [kabod], and the lifter up [rum] of mine head [rosh].
3.notes: ve-attah YHWH -- 'but You' -- the Psalter's great pivot. magen baadi (H4043), a shield AROUND me, the margin's 'about'; kebodi (H3519), my glory, for a king who had just lost his city; u-merim roshi (H7311, H7218), the lifter of my head -- the head Absalom's coup had bowed. Every loss of that night reversed in three titles.

4.text: With my voice I cry to the LORD, and He answers me from His holy hill. Selah.
4.amp: I cried [qara] unto the LORD [YHWH] with my voice [qol], and He heard ['answered', anah] me out of His holy [qodesh] hill [har]. Selah.
4.notes: qoli el-YHWH eqra (H6963, H7121), with my voice I cry to the LORD -- audible prayer, a voice in the dark -- and va-yaaneni (H6030), He answers, me-har qodsho (H2022, H6944), from His holy hill: Zion, the very hill David had just fled. The ark stayed in the city (cf. 2 Samuel 15:25); the God of the ark went with the fugitive.

5.text: I laid myself down and slept; I woke again, for the LORD keeps upholding me.
5.amp: I laid me down [shakab] and slept [yashen]; I awaked [quts]; for the LORD [YHWH] sustained [samak -- upheld, propped] me.
5.notes: The claim everyone quotes, made on the run: ani shakhavti va-ishanah, heqitsoti (H7901, H3462, H6974) -- lay down, slept, woke. The reason is samak (H5564), the leaning-verb: the LORD is what David leaned on through the night. Sleep as an act of faith (cf. Psalm 4:8; Mark 4:38).

6.text: I will not be afraid of tens of thousands of people who have set themselves against me on every side.
6.amp: I will not be afraid [yare] of ten thousands [rebabah] of people [am], that have set [shith] themselves against me round about [sabib].
6.notes: lo-ira me-rivevot am (H3372, H7233, H5971), I will not fear the tens of thousands -- and the tens of thousands are Absalom's Israel (cf. 2 Samuel 17:11, 'all Israel gathered as the sand'); shith sabib (H7896, H5439), deployed on every side. The arithmetic of verse 1 has grown; the fear has not.

7.text: Rise up, O LORD! Save me, O my God! For You have struck all my enemies on the jaw; You have shattered the teeth of the wicked.
7.amp: Arise [qum], O LORD [YHWH]; save [yasha] me, O my God [Elohim]: for You have smitten [nakah] all mine enemies [oyeb] upon the cheek bone [lechi -- jaw]; You have broken [shabar] the teeth [shen] of the ungodly [rasha].
7.notes: qumah YHWH (H6965) -- the war-cry of the ark's marching (cf. Numbers 10:35), answering the 'rising up' of the enemies in verse 1. The imagery is a brawl: hikkita lechi (H5221, H3895), a blow to the jaw; shinne reshaim shibbarta (H8127, H7563, H7665), the teeth of the wicked broken -- predators defanged, not merely defeated.

8.text: Salvation belongs to the LORD; may Your blessing rest upon Your people. Selah.
8.amp: Salvation [yeshuah] belongs unto the LORD [YHWH]: Your blessing [berakah] is upon Your people [am]. Selah.
8.notes: la-YHWH ha-yeshuah (H3444): the verse-2 word thrown back -- they said there was no salvation for him in God; there is, and it is God's to give. Then the widening: al-ammekha birkhatekha (H5971, H1293), Your blessing on Your people -- the king prays for the very people who followed Absalom. Jonah prays this line from inside the fish (cf. Jonah 2:9).
